title: Sunbathing
description: An American alligator (Alligator mississippiensis) lies on a log amongst ancient water tupelos (Nyssa aquatica) in the Beidler Forest in Harleyville, South Carolina. Light barely penetrates beneath the dense canopy of the old growth forest, but ectotherms like alligators and turtles find adequate sunbathing locations in areas where trees cannot grow.
translated_description: 一只美洲短吻鳄（Alligator mississippiensis）躺在南卡罗来纳州哈利维尔贝德勒森林中古老的水紫树（Nyssa aquatica）之间的原木上。光线几乎无法穿透这片原始森林茂密的树冠，但像短吻鳄和龟类这样的变温动物在树木无法生长的区域找到了充足的日光浴场所。
